info.summary: Curriculum content, learner progress and reports over HTTP.

get.description:
Level -> module -> lesson tree with the caller's states (``rc roadmap``).

Lesson state: done, in_progress or available. Module state: done if every lesson is done,
in_progress if any is started or done, else available. Progress values are fractions (0-1).
Nothing is ever `locked` — lessons are not gated on finishing other lessons (ADR 0015);
the value stays in the enum so an existing client keeps parsing.

Every lesson's progress in teaching order, the running timer, and the dashboard numbers.

The dashboard part (``stages``, ``week``, ``streak_days``, ``due_cards``) is the same
aggregate the static site and ``rc status`` show, and covers every course even when
``course`` narrows the lesson list.
Lessons whose prerequisites are done: in-progress first, then teaching order.

so they are now next in the recommended order. They were never blocked (ADR 0015).

post.description: Create a local account (role learner) and mail an email-verification link.

Start a browser session. Five failures in 15 minutes lock the account temporarily.

With ``remember`` the cookies last as long as the session may stay idle; without it they
end when the browser is closed.
End this browser session (needs the CSRF header).

Send the verification link again to the signed-in account's own address.

Needs a session, so there is nothing to enumerate and no address to type. 503 when the
server has no SMTP configuration — the client reads `email_verification` first and does
not offer this at all in that case. Already-verified accounts get 202 and no mail.
Confirm the email address with the mailed one-time token (valid 24 hours).

Mail a reset link (valid 30 minutes, single use) if the account exists.

The answer is the same whether or not the email is registered.
Set a new password with a reset token; every session of the account is ended.

get.description:

frontend reads as "show no provider buttons".

get.description:
CPU, memory, disk, temperature, uptime and database readings, taken now.

Read from the machine the API runs on. In a container the load, memory and temperature
are the host's and the disk is the data volume. A reading the host does not expose is
null or absent rather than a guess.

API requests over a period: volume, success rate, latency, and the routes behind them.

The success rate is ``1 - 5xx / all``: a 4xx is the caller's mistake and is reported
beside it, not counted against the service. Latency quantiles are estimated from a
histogram, so they are accurate to its bucket edges.

Requests that failed on the server's side (5xx), newest first.

Each carries the request id: the full stack trace is in the server log under the same id.

Page views and unique visitors per day, the most viewed pages and where visits came from.

Days are in the service's time zone (``RC_TIMEZONE``, Korea Standard Time by default). A
visitor is counted once per day by a pseudonym that changes daily, so the
daily figures are exact and their sum is *visitor-days*, not unique people over the range.
Signed-in accounts active in the last 7 and 30 days come from the audit log instead.

Product KPIs: active users, growth, activation and retention, and learning volume.

- **Active users** come from session activity: an account counts when one of its sessions
  was used in the period. Stickiness is DAU / MAU.
- **Activation** is the share of accounts created in the last 30 days that completed at
  least one lesson. **Week-1 retention** is the share of accounts created 7 to 14 days ago
  that were active again in the last 7 days.
- **Visit to sign-up** divides sign-ups by visitor-days; it shows the trend, not a funnel,
  because a visitor is only recognisable within one day (ADR 0017).

post.description:
Count one page view.

Stored: the day, the normalized path, the language, whether the client is automated,
whether the reader is signed in, and the referring host. The address and user agent are
used once, to derive a visitor pseudonym that changes every day, and are not stored.

403 unless the caller is the web tier; 404 when monitoring is off.

ActivityKind.title: ActivityKind
ActivityKind.description:
What kind of work an activity is.

``reading`` is a textbook or notes; ``paper`` is a primary paper read with notes of one's
own, which the research track has to tell apart from it. ``exercise`` is a problem set,
``reproduction`` is reproducing a published result, and ``project`` is a capstone.
See ``research_notes/연구 트랙 설계/lesson-standard.md`` §11-2.
